Cross polinisation. Has a lot to do with it as covered above. In particular the RN has had the most influence. Due to the empire, when counties started to break off they pretty much adopted the RN uniform with minor modifications. Despite their probable protests this includes the USN. This established the de-facto standard of what a naval uniform should look like.

As to the basic colour scheme, most military uniforms are derived from a large part heraldic traditions and blue is a fairly obvious symbol for a seafaring force. The gold of rank and epaulettes and rank hasn't got a particular meaning that I'm aware of, just looks awfully sharp on a blue background. Status probably had something to do with it as officers were largely drawn from the nobility as late as the early 20th century. Rank markings were made of actual gold back then.

Mid 20th century, most western navies transitioned from blue to black uniforms. This had a combination of factors; availability of fabric, influence of rising US power, and generally sharper looking uniform.
